Let me address the meat of your post with one sentence: This is what a labor surplus looks like.

Labor, like any other good in a free market, is priced based on supply/demand. In this case, the supply is very rigid. People most work or they don't get to eat. So if the demand for labor goes down this leads to a drop in price. Because roofs aren't getting cheaper, people have to work more to get the same amount of money. Which means the supply goes up even more!

This isn't the first time this has happened. When machines replaced farmers the exact same problem happened. The millenia-old solution was to wage a war so the population dwindles down. Thus World War 1. Only it didn't kill enough. Spanish Flu killed more people, mostly soldering age too, and that still wasn't enough. Thus came the Great Depression and later World War 2. We tried job rationing here in the states and for the most part it worked, but it took a long time for the market to equalize out.

We're seeing history repeat right before our eyes. We have a labor surplus thanks to automation. This is leading to increased unrest (Arab Spring is just one example) around the world. We need to address the labor surplus with serious solutions. Programs to increase jobs clearly aren't working as the OP's comic shows. Basic Income would essentially be gifting everyone some of the benefits of this automation. We already give everyone free education. Basic Income would support the same ideas that free education does.
